question: Are there any red flags in Apple's financial statements?

answer.summary: Apple's FY2023 financial statements received an unqualified audit opinion [T00627], but the year showed broad-based slowdowns. Revenue fell 2.8% to $383.29B [F00013], and operating income declined 4.3% to $114.30B [F00037]. Operating cash flow dropped 9.5% to $110.54B [F00224], dragging free cash flow down 10.6% to $99.58B [F01389]. Liquidity remains tight with a current ratio of 0.99 in FY2023 [F01421], below the 1.0 threshold. Inventory grew 28% while cost of revenue fell 4% [F00099] [F00022], suggesting potential build-up risk. Shareholder payouts consumed 93% of FY2023 free cash flow [F01448] [F01389], limiting downside absorption.
drivers: Revenue contraction [F00013] coincides with operating income decline [F00037].
Free cash flow decline [F01389] tracks operating cash flow decline [F00224] as capex remained stable [F00236].
High shareholder payout ratio [F01448] reduces retained cash buffer.
risks_and_red_flags: Current ratio below 1.0 in FY2023 (0.99) [F01421] and FY2022 (0.88) [F01420].
Inventory grew 28% in FY2023 while cost of revenue fell 4% [F00099] [F00022].
Shareholder payouts consumed 93% of FY2023 free cash flow [F01448] [F01389].
Interest coverage fell 29% to 29.1x in FY2023 [F01432].
Revenue and operating income declined in FY2023 [F00013] [F00037].
Operating cash flow fell 9.5% in FY2023 [F00224].
data_quality_notes: 3 accounting identities passed, 0 failed for the numbers above.
Operating cash flow and capex figures are XBRL-tagged [F00224] [F00236].

outlook.actuals_view: FY2023 showed a slowdown with revenue down 2.8% [F00013] and free cash flow down 10.6% [F01389] compared to FY2022.

follow_up_checks: Verify inventory aging and obsolescence reserves given 28% growth vs -4% cost of revenue [F00099] [F00022].
Review segment revenue mix to identify drivers of the 2.8% revenue decline [F00013].
Check debt maturity schedule given the 29% interest coverage drop [F01432].
Assess sustainability of the 93% payout ratio against free cash flow volatility [F01448] [F01389].
